about: Byte-exact vectors for Occulta's wire and at-rest formats. Each vector holds its inputs and the exact bytes they must produce. Expected values were recorded from the Swift implementation and are never edited: a change that alters one breaks compatibility with every contact still producing or reading those bytes. Add a vector for a new format; do not change an old one. All binary values are lowercase hex. Dates are seconds since 2001-01-01T00:00:00Z, which is also how Foundation's JSONEncoder writes a Date by default; SignedAttribute signing payloads instead write whole Unix-epoch seconds, truncated. JSON objects are written with sorted keys. fsKey inputs are P-256 private scalars; public keys are scalar times G in X9.63 form. ECDH output is SHA-256(Z || 00000001), the X9.63 KDF that SecKeyCopyKeyExchangeResult applies with a 32-byte requested size and no shared info, before HKDF.

vectors.name: ltKey.classical
vectors.note: Long-term identity key: HKDF-SHA256(ikm: ecdhOutput, salt: own XOR peer public key (x963), info: 'Occulta-v1-transport-2025'). ecdhOutput is the X9.63-KDF output, as for fsKey.

vectors.name: ltKey.hybrid
vectors.note: As ltKey.classical, with ikm: ecdhOutput || sorted(encapsulatedSecret, decapsulatedSecret) and info: 'Occulta-v2-hybrid-pq-transport-2026'.

vectors.name: diceware
vectors.note: As ltKey.hybrid, with info: 'Occulta-v2-diceware-2026' || sorted(ourNonce, peerNonce).

vectors.name: card.v1.longTermKey
vectors.note: SPEC §3. The long-term slot key between two card agreement keys: the derivation of ltKey.hybrid, with the card keys in place of the identity keys.

vectors.name: recipientPayload.introduction
vectors.note: SPEC §4.4. Carol's bootstrap payload: the introduction rides in RecipientPayload.introduction, encoded with its binary fields as base64 like every other Data. cardDigest is not part of the payload (it only feeds the signature, which is an input here); it is given so the vector shares the introduction shape.

vectors.name: card.v1.encoding
vectors.note: SPEC §2. The keys are given X9.63 (65 bytes) and written as their 64 bytes after the 0x04 prefix. expiresAtUnix is Unix seconds (not the 2001 epoch the other vectors use), written UInt64 big-endian at offset 128 and XORed with the first 8 bytes of SHA-256 of the 64-byte agreement key. The signature is an input: signatures are random, so the vector pins the layout, not the signing.

vectors.name: card.v1.signingPayload
vectors.note: SPEC §2. 'Occulta-introduction-card-v1' followed by the first 1704 bytes of the layout: the two keys without their 0x04 prefix, the masked expiry, the ML-KEM key. expiresAtUnix is Unix seconds.

vectors.name: card.v1.introduction.signingPayload
vectors.note: SPEC §4.4. 'Occulta-card-introduction-v1' followed by the digest of the card being answered, then the three keys.

vectors.name: card.v1.bootstrapKey.carol
vectors.note: SPEC §4.3. K_inner for Carol's bootstrap slots: HKDF-SHA256(ikm: ecdhOutput || ss1, salt: peer XOR own, info: 'Occulta-v2-card-bootstrap-2026'). ecdhOutput is the X9.63-KDF output, as for fsKey.

vectors.name: card.v1.bootstrapLayer
vectors.note: SPEC §4.3. AES-GCM(outerKey, mlkemCiphertext || AES-GCM(innerKey, payload, AAD: blind || mlkemCiphertext), AAD: blind), both combined as nonce || ciphertext || tag. payload is the ASCII of 'card bootstrap payload'.

vectors.name: card.v1.meeting.transcript
vectors.note: SPEC §7. SHA-256('Occulta-card-meeting-v1' || sorted ids || sorted nonces || sorted ciphertexts), every element framed as UInt16 big-endian length || bytes. The first id and the first ciphertext are given the larger way round on purpose; the nonces are already in order.

vectors.name: card.v1.field.empty
vectors.note: SPEC §5. The card field's plaintext before sealing: 0x01, UInt32 big-endian payload length, binary plist of the empty state, zeros to 12288 bytes.

vectors.name: challenge.v1.field.empty
vectors.note: Bug 180. The challenge column's plaintext before sealing: 0x01, slot count 33, 14 zeros, then 33 slots of 64 zeros, 2128 bytes.

vectors.name: challenge.v1.field.slot1
vectors.note: Bug 180. Depth 1 holds a challenge and a verified-at, no other slot does: flags 0x03, nonce, issuedAt and verifiedAt as UInt64 big-endian, 15 zeros, at offset 16 + 1 * 64.
